title: Evolution in neuropsychiatric cis-regulatory enhancers through human-specific neuronal mutations within transcription factor binding sites.
authors: Raza, Rabail Zehra; Raza, Saad; Naveed, Sumayyah; Ali, Shahid
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Proteins and proteomics
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过分子动力学模拟分析神经精神疾病增强子中人类特异性突变对转录因子结合亲和力的影响，聚焦TF-DNA互作机制，但对象为疾病相关增强子而非典型TF-DNA结合位点预测，方法以MD为主，整体匹配度中等偏上。
abstract: cis-Regulatory elements (CREs) in multicellular genomes play a significant role in precise regulation of the genes. Increasing evidence has shown that alterations in CREs have had a drastic effect on the human brain evolution, neuronal cell adaptation and physiology. The human-specific sequence acceleration in CREs has not only changed the overall cognitive function of the human brain, but also seems to have strongly increased the risk of developing psychiatric disorders. Mapping the human-specific neuronal mutations within CREs remains to be a challenge and can largely impact the way DNA binding domain of the transcription factors interact with the CREs. In this study, we have identified human-specific neuronal mutations within transcription factor binding sites in neuropsychiatric enhancers of three major psychiatric disorders i.e. autism spectrum disorder, schizophrenia and bipolar disorder and studied the impact of human-specific neuronal mutations on binding affinities with the respective transcription factors via molecular dynamic simulation. Moreover, we have also identified signals of positive selection in the same set of empirically confirmed neuropsychiatric enhancers and correlated it with the way transcription factors bind with the human-specific and their counterpart ancestral allele harboring transcription factor binding sites.
abstract_zh: 多细胞基因组中的顺式调控元件（cis-Regulatory Elements, CREs）在基因的精确调控中发挥着重要作用。越来越多的证据表明，CREs的改变对人类大脑进化、神经元细胞适应及生理功能产生了显著影响。CREs中人类特异性序列的加速变化不仅改变了人类大脑的整体认知功能，而且似乎也显著增加了患精神疾病的风险。在CREs内定位人类特异性神经元突变仍是一个挑战，这可能极大地影响转录因子DNA结合域与CREs的相互作用方式。在本研究中，我们识别了三种主要精神疾病（即自闭症谱系障碍、精神分裂症和双相情感障碍）的神经精神增强子中转录因子结合位点内的人类特异性神经元突变，并通过分子动力学模拟研究了这些人类特异性神经元突变对与相应转录因子结合亲和力的影响。此外，我们还在同一组经实验验证的神经精神增强子中识别了正选择信号，并将其与转录因子结合人类特异性及对应祖先等位基因携带的转录因子结合位点的方式相关联。
